n7cb14c3fae3.s: While the Vice-President acts as President, who presides over the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
n7cb14c3fae3.x: While acting as President, the Vice-President stops functioning as Chairman and the Deputy Chairman presides. (Sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates.)

nindian-polity-9-12.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tie in the Rajya Sabha – Vice-President has no vote
Resolution for his own removal – Vice-President presides
Re-election of the Vice-President – any number of times
Vote of the Vice-President – on every motion in the first instance
nindian-polity-9-12.x: The Vice-President can be re-elected any number of times. He has only a casting vote in a tie and does not preside while his own removal is considered.

nindian-polity-45-2.s: The Parliament of India consists of:
o: The Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha only
The President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
The President, the Vice-President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
The Vice-President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
nindian-polity-45-2.x: Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. The Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha but is not a constituent part of Parliament.

nindian-polity-7-12.s: Who among the following can ask any Union Minister to resign?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-7-12.x: As head of the Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister selects Ministers, allocates portfolios and can ask any Minister to resign.

nindian-polity-56-14.s: Under which Article do the Chief Minister and State Ministers take the oath of office and secrecy?
nindian-polity-56-14.x: The Chief Minister and State Ministers take their oaths under Article 164(3); Article 75(4) is for Union Ministers and Article 159 for the Governor.

n3b154351943.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Prime Minister is correctly matched?
o: Oath of the PM – administered by the Chief Justice of India
Membership at appointment – must be a Lok Sabha member
A non-member PM – must enter Parliament within one year
n3b154351943.x: The President appoints the PM under Article 75(1) and administers his oath. The PM may belong to either House, and a non-member gets six months to become an MP.

n59d62d3918f.s: Which case held that a non-member cannot be repeatedly reappointed as a Minister without getting elected?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab
n59d62d3918f.x: In S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001) the Supreme Court held that the non-member provision cannot be used for repeated reappointments without election.

n0bdc0557043.s: Unlike the UK Prime Minister, who must belong to the House of Commons, the Indian Prime Minister may belong to:
n0bdc0557043.x: The UK Prime Minister must be in the House of Commons, while the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.

nindian-polity-7-5.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Inter-State Council, as well as NITI Aayog, the National Development Council and the National Integration Council.

nindian-polity-7-13.s: Which Article lays down the duties of the Prime Minister towards the President?
nindian-polity-7-13.x: The PM's duties to communicate decisions and furnish information to the President are in Article 78; Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise.

nindian-polity-7-16.s: On whose advice does the President appoint the other Union Ministers?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-7-16.x: The PM advises the President on appointing Ministers and on dissolving the Lok Sabha; the CJI is appointed through the collegium process, not on the PM's advice.

n74969792cf4.s: Which Article provides that the advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into by any court?
n74969792cf4.x: Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice; Article 77 deals with action in the President's name, authentication of orders and business rules.

n41c47e78c3b.s: Under Article 164(1A), what is the maximum number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a 294-member Assembly?
n41c47e78c3b.x: 15% of 294 is 44.1, so the maximum is 44 (e.g. West Bengal), not 45.

nindian-polity-31-4.s: The Attorney General of India holds office:
o: For a fixed term of five years
During the pleasure of the President
For a fixed term of six years
nindian-polity-31-4.x: The Attorney General serves during the President's pleasure, so the Constitution gives him no fixed tenure.

nindian-polity-31-7.s: In Parliament, the Attorney General of India CANNOT:
o: Vote on a motion or bill
Enjoy the privileges of an MP under Article 105(4)
Take part in the proceedings of the Houses
nindian-polity-31-7.x: The Attorney General can speak in either House and enjoys MPs' privileges under Article 105(4), but he has no right to vote.

nindian-polity-31-13.s: Legal duties are referred to the Attorney General of India by the:
nindian-polity-31-13.x: The Attorney General performs legal duties referred by the President, not by a Governor; the State's legal adviser is the Advocate General.

nindian-polity-32-5.s: Under Article 177, the Advocate General of a State CANNOT:
o: Be named a member of a Legislative committee
nindian-polity-32-5.x: Article 177 lets the Advocate General speak in both Houses and sit on committees, but he cannot vote.

n785a464778b.s: Which restriction applies to the Attorney General of India?
o: He cannot take up private practice
He cannot advise or brief against the Government of India
He must serve as a full-time officer
He can never become a company director
n785a464778b.x: Private practice is permitted and the office is not full-time, but the Attorney General cannot advise or brief against the Government of India; a directorship needs permission.

n634f2279a8f.s: The Shadow Cabinet is a feature associated with:
n634f2279a8f.x: The Shadow Cabinet is associated with the United Kingdom; India has no formal counterpart.

nindian-polity-9-16.s: Which of the following is an integral part of the Parliament of India?
nindian-polity-9-16.x: The President is an integral part of Parliament (Article 79); the Vice-President, though Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, is not a part of Parliament.

n02ee91632a7.s: Which of the following is cited as an argument against a second chamber?
o: It gives a second examination to every Bill
It brings in experts through nomination
n02ee91632a7.x: Delay and duplication are cited against a second chamber; a double check, regional representation and expert nomination are arguments in its favour.

nf23467a1f86.s: A bicameral State Legislature consists of:
o: The Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council only
The Governor and the Legislative Assembly
The Governor, the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council
The Governor and the Legislative Council
nf23467a1f86.x: A bicameral legislature is Governor + Assembly + Council; a unicameral one is Governor + Assembly.

nindian-polity-62-37.s: How many States in India have bicameral legislatures?
nindian-polity-62-37.x: Six States are bicameral: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh.

n6b55af108ea.s: The Legislative Assembly of Delhi is based on:
n6b55af108ea.x: Delhi's Assembly rests on Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Amendment (1991); Puducherry's rests on Article 239A.

new.s: Which Prime Minister had the shortest tenure, 13 days in 1996?
new.x: A.B. Vajpayee's 1996 tenure of 13 days is the shortest; Nanda was acting PM and Charan Singh never faced the Lok Sabha.

new.s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India from South India?
new.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao became PM in 1991 without being an MP and was the first PM from South India.

new.s: Union Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the:
new.x: Under Article 75(2) Ministers hold office at the President's pleasure, not legally the PM's; the President removes a Minister only on the PM's advice.

new.s: Ministers who head their own ministry without Cabinet rank are called:
o: Ministers of State attached to Cabinet Ministers
new.x: Ministers of State with independent charge hold their own ministry; Deputy Ministers only assist and Cabinet Ministers have Cabinet rank.

new.s: The Allocation of Business Rules and the Transaction of Business Rules, made under Article 77(3), date from:
new.x: Both sets of Rules were made in 1961 under Article 77(3); the President allocates portfolios on the PM's advice.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 74?
o: Article 74(1) provides a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
The President may ask for reconsideration of advice once
Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice
Article 74(3) lays down the duties of the Prime Minister
new.x: Article 74(3) does not exist; the PM's duties to the President are in Article 78.

new.s: With a Lok Sabha of 543 members, the Union Council of Ministers, including the PM, can have at most:
new.x: Article 75(1A) caps Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha's strength: 15% of 543 gives a maximum of 81.

new.s: When both Houses are full, the electoral college for the Vice-President has how many members?
new.x: All 788 MPs, elected and nominated, elect the Vice-President; State Legislatures have no role.

new.s: Disputes regarding the election of the Vice-President are decided by the:
new.x: Under Article 71 all disputes over the Vice-President's election are decided finally by the Supreme Court.

new.s: The form of oath of the Vice-President is laid down in:
new.x: The oaths of the President, Vice-President and Governor are written in Articles 60, 69 and 159, not in the Third Schedule, which holds ministers' oaths.

new.s: A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be moved only after a notice of at least:
new.x: The removal resolution needs 14 days' notice, is moved only in the Rajya Sabha and must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

new.s: Which future Vice-President had earlier been India's Ambassador to the USSR?
new.x: S. Radhakrishnan was Ambassador to the USSR (1949–52) before becoming the first VP; V.V. Giri served in Sri Lanka and K.R. Narayanan in China.

new.s: M. Venkaiah Naidu of Andhra Pradesh served as Vice-President during:
new.x: M. Venkaiah Naidu (Nellore) was Vice-President from 2017 to 2022.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Prime Minister:
1. The post is not mentioned in the Constitution.
2. He takes the oath as an ordinary Minister.
3. He enjoys the powers of the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Deputy PM is not a constitutional post and is sworn in as an ordinary Minister; he has no PM powers, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
new.x: The PM was ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission; its first Deputy Chairman, of Cabinet rank, was Gulzarilal Nanda.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 75(3) – Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
new.x: Article 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; 75(2) is the President's pleasure, 75(1A) the size cap and 77(3) the business rules.

new.s: A Minister who has resigned may explain his resignation in the House through a personal statement with the consent of the:
new.x: A resigned minister may make a personal statement explaining his resignation with the Speaker's consent.

new.s: In practice, who can ask a Union Minister to resign or advise the President to dismiss him?
new.x: Ministers hold office at the President's pleasure, but in practice the PM can ask a minister to resign or advise his dismissal.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 75(2) – Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
new.x: Article 75(2) is individual responsibility (President's pleasure); 75(3) is collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha, and 164(2) applies it to the State Assembly.

new.s: Which Cabinet Committee decided on caste enumeration in the Census in April 2025?
new.x: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, the 'super cabinet', decided caste enumeration in the Census on 30 April 2025 – not the CCEA.

new.s: Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Accommodation (2024)?
new.x: Amit Shah chairs the Accommodation committee and Rajnath Singh the Parliamentary Affairs committee; these two are not chaired by the PM.

new.s: The office of the Solicitor General of India is based on:
new.x: The Solicitor General is non-constitutional; Article 76 is the Attorney General and Article 165 the Advocate General.

new.s: Who was the first Solicitor General of India?
new.x: C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General; M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General.

new.s: The Solicitor General of India is appointed by the:
new.x: The Solicitor General is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet for 3 years; the Attorney General is appointed by the President.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Council of Ministers and the Cabinet:
1. The Council of Ministers rarely meets as a body.
2. The Cabinet directs and supervises the Council of Ministers.
3. The word 'Cabinet' appears in Article 74.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Council rarely meets as a body and the Cabinet directs it. The word 'Cabinet' appears only in Article 352(3), so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: The Cabinet Secretary is appointed for an initial term of:
new.x: The ACC appoints the Cabinet Secretary for 2 years, extendable up to 4.

new.s: To be appointed Attorney General of India, a person must be qualified to be appointed a:
o: Chief Justice of a High Court
new.x: Under Article 76 the Attorney General must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge; his remuneration is fixed by the President.

new.s: Who has been the Attorney General of India since 1 October 2022?
new.x: R. Venkataramani succeeded K.K. Venugopal on 1 October 2022 and was re-appointed from 1 October 2025.

new.s: The Parliament of Japan is known as the:
new.x: Japan's Parliament is the National Diet; the Knesset is Israel's, the Federal Assembly Russia's and Congress the USA's.

new.s: In Russia's Federal Assembly, the lower House is the:
new.x: The State Duma is the lower House and the Federation Council the upper House of Russia's Federal Assembly.

new.s: The upper House of Japan's National Diet is the:
new.x: Japan's upper House is the House of Councillors; its lower House is the House of Representatives.

new.s: The allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to the States is given in the:
new.x: Rajya Sabha seats are allotted by population in the Fourth Schedule, unlike the equal representation in the US Senate.

new.s: In the US Senate, each state is represented by:
new.x: The US Senate gives equal representation – 2 per state (100 in all) – and has no nominated members.

new.s: A State Legislative Council is created or abolished by:
o: A law of Parliament under Article 169
new.x: Under Article 169 Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law after an Assembly resolution; it is not an Article 368 amendment.

new.s: Which country's unicameral legislature, with 2,977 members, is the biggest Parliament?
new.x: China's National People's Congress, with 2,977 members, is the biggest Parliament.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the second chamber:
1. Abbé Sieyès called it superfluous if it agrees and mischievous if it dissents.
2. N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar defended the Rajya Sabha as a House of dignified debate.
3. A second chamber speeds up law-making.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A second chamber causes delay and duplication; it does not speed up law-making.

new.s: How many members does Jammu and Kashmir elect to the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: Only Delhi (3), Puducherry (1) and Jammu and Kashmir (4) among the UTs elect Rajya Sabha members.
